text:
maria (support): Hey team — ACME reported streaming answers cut off mid-event and client never gets the final 'data: [DONE]'. They see a 502 from their corporate proxy, then client reconnects and creates duplicate billing entries. Repro on their Dedicated private cluster behind VPC + corp-proxy. Any quick theory?

srinivas (oncall): Do we have the original request headers + client curl? Is this HTTP/1.1 SSE or HTTP/2?
maria (support): They said SSE over HTTP/1.1. Sending this sample they used to reproduce:

```bash
curl -v -N -H "Authorization: Bearer *****" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  "https://dedicated.acme.redwood/api/v1/stream?model=gpt-fine-rt"
```

maria (support): Attached message from their logs:

```
[2026-03-12T15:22:10Z] upstream error: 502, corpproxy closed connection while streaming chunked body
[2026-03-12T15:22:10Z] last successful chunk id: 0x4f2a, partial chunk len: 648
```

ryan (network): That "partial chunk len" line screams MTU/MSS fragmentation to me — proxy/firewall drops fragments so the chunked transfer gets truncated. Do we have a packet capture?
dan (eng-infra): We asked for pcap; customer attached tcpdump showing repeated ICMP "Fragmentation needed" from their firewall. Snippet:

```
12:22:09.123456 IP 10.0.0.5 > 198.51.100.1: Flags [P.], seq 12345:13093, ack 54321, win 29200, length 648
12:22:09.123457 ICMP 198.51.100.254 unreachable - need to frag (MTU 1400)
12:22:09.123459 IP 10.0.0.5 > 198.51.100.1: Flags [P.], seq 13093:13741, ack 54321, win 29200, length 648 (retransmit)
```

ryan (network): Their VPC path supports 1500, but corporate edge clamps MSS or blocks ICMP PMTU messages. If the server sends 1500-byte segments with DF bit set, intermediate proxy blocks fragments -> chunk cut.
srinivas (oncall): So streaming chunk boundary splits mid-SSE frame, the proxy sees an incomplete chunk and tears down after timeout. Explains missing final [DONE].
maria (support): Customer also said their corporate proxy rewrites chunk sizes (some proxies buffer entire responses and re-chunk). Could that interplay cause duplicate partial deliveries on reconnect?
dan (eng-infra): Yes — two failure modes:
- PMTU blackhole (fragments dropped) -> truncated chunk -> proxy errors out.
- Proxy buffering + http-server-close behavior -> it will cache partial body and on client reconnect may replay partial/new chunks leading to duplicates or missing terminator.

ryan (network): Quick repro steps for customer to try:
1) On their edge firewall/router, enable MSS-clamping to 1400 for TCP flows to our egress IPs OR reduce server-side MTU to 1400 for the node group.
2) Allow ICMP type 3/code 4 (Fragmentation Needed) so PMTU can converge.
3) Turn off buffering at the corporate proxy for the SSE path (nginx: `proxy_buffering off; proxy_request_buffering off;`), or ensure `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` is preserved.

srinivas (oncall): Dan, can we surface a quick-run checklist for Support to share with customers? Small safe changes first: set `proxy_buffering off`, add keepalive headers, lower MTU on nodes temporarily.
dan (eng-infra): I'll draft a checklist. Also an immediate mitigation server-side: we can switch SSE responses to smaller chunks (reduce chunk size to ~512 bytes) for that customer via route override to avoid fragmentation. That avoids customer network changes while they fix infra.
maria (support): Nice. Customer asked for exact headers we need. Dan—what headers will help proxies treat stream as truly streaming?
dan (eng-infra): Recommend adding:
- `Connection: keep-alive`
- `Cache-Control: no-transform, no-store`
- `X-Accel-Buffering: no` (for nginx)
- `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` (already set)
These reduce proxy buffering and transformation.

deploy-bot: deployment 2026-03-12T16:00 triggered: route-override/acme-small-chunks -> canary on 2 nodes.

maria (support): I'll send the checklist + temporary route-override option to ACME and ask them to test 1) MSS clamping or 2) apply our canary that uses 512B chunking.

ryan (network): Also log to capture for us: full tcpdump of a failing session (client->edge->our node) + the corpproxy headers (via debug logs). Without ICMP it's hard to prove PMTU blackhole.
srinivas (oncall): Marking for follow-up: if canary reduces failures, escalate to infra to support low-chunk profile permanently for customers behind flaky proxies.
maria (support): Thanks all — filing ticket with customer notes + assigned eng-infra. Will update thread when they test canary. :thumbsup:
